key_insight: Localizing medical evaluation rubrics for Japan exposes item-level scoring errors that stable overall LLM rankings can hide.
clinical_relevance: Japan-specific rubrics can better recognize responses suited to local healthcare systems, medications, and care pathways.
method: Localized 79 HealthBench consultations with 1,022 evaluation criteria.
Combined source-cited LLM drafts with specialist revision, independent dual-physician review, and meta-review.
Compared localized and machine-translated rubrics across 18 LLMs.
evidence_signal: Despite strong ranking agreement (τ=0.817), localization flipped verdicts on 17.7% of modified criteria versus 7.3% re-grading noise and reduced false penalties on Japan-adapted negative criteria by 7.1 percentage points.
watch_item: Results cover 79 consultations and benchmark scoring, not demonstrated safety or effectiveness in clinical practice.
paper_title: JHealthBench-L: Clinician-Reviewed Localization of HealthBench for Rubric-Based Medical LLM Evaluation in Japan
